agent left out.effect: Bulk driving force (a tilt from supersaturation or undercooling)
agent left out.why: It is zero at coexistence by assumption.

agent left out.effect: Coupling to vapor density and temperature
agent left out.why: Temperature is uniform and the vapor is at saturation, so these fields add no energy that depends on phi here. That coupling is handled in other tasks.

agent left out.effect: Regolith grain phase and wetting energies between ice and grain or gas and grain
agent left out.why: The work order treats only the ice-gas pore space.

agent left out.effect: Anisotropy of the ice surface energy
agent left out.why: Assumed isotropic. Ice anisotropy is a few percent at most for rough surfaces near 200 K.

agent left out.effect: Elastic strain energy in the ice
agent left out.why: There is no stress model, and grains are assumed not to constrain the ice.
The deliverable excludes them. They change the energy at relative order (eps/R)^2 for an interface with radius of curvature R much larger than eps.
